description: Verify that DUT replies to an ARP Request whose target_hw is the broadcast MAC ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff — broadcast in target_hw is unusual but RFC 826 §2.4 still requires reply if target_ip matches us
approach:
[Objective]
Some stacks fill target_hw with the broadcast address rather than leaving it zero. The resolver semantics are unchanged — what matters per RFC 826 §2.4 is whether target_ip matches the receiver. DUT must reply.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request injected
   • opcode      = 1
   • target_hw   = ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff   ← broadcast in the field; should be ignored by resolver
   • target_ip   = DUT IP
   • sender_*    = HOST-1-IP / MAC-ADDR1

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: ARP Reply (opcode 2, sender_mac=DUT, target_ip=HOST-1-IP)

[Pass condition]
DUT emits an ARP Reply within the observation window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_no_reply — DUT did not reply. The receiver should not condition reply behaviour on target_hw — only on target_ip per RFC 826 §2.4.

verdicts.Pass: DUT replied — target_hw=broadcast was tolerated correctly
verdicts.Fail_no_reply: DUT did not reply — receiver wrongly conditioned on target_hw value
